mainTopic: Does a second נזירות or שבועה take effect on top of an existing one? The defense of רב הונא, and רבא's rule that a second שבועה takes effect once the first is released.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a challenge to רב הונא, who holds that saying 'הריני נזיר היום' twice does not create a second נזירות. The גמרא defends him: the earlier source can be read as 'today, tomorrow' or as two נזירות taken on at once. רב המנונא then brings a ברייתא that learns from 'נזיר להזיר' that נזירות takes effect on נזירות. The גמרא argues that this must be about 'today, today', but answers that it too is about two נזירות accepted together. Next the גמרא asks why a שבועה counts as stricter than a נדר, and concludes it is because the תורה says 'לֹא יְנַקֶּה' about a שבועה. Then it turns to the משנה: two identical שבועות not to eat bring only one liability. רבא rules that if the first שבועה is released, the second takes effect, and the גמרא gives two versions of how this comes from the משנה's wording. A case of two נזירות seems to support רבא, but the גמרא pushes the proof away, since there both were accepted at once.

steps.title: The earlier challenge ends: a refutation of רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its previous argument by declaring that the source refutes רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an argument that began before this section. It declares that the source it just brought seems to knock down רב הונא's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier source said that when a person has his first נזירות cancelled, the second one 'counts for him.' The גמרא read this as a case where he said 'today' twice, so it seemed to prove that a second נזירות takes effect, which goes against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: A strong refutation, a challenge that seems to knock down a view
The אמורא whose view is being challenged here

phrases.english: And this is a refutation of Rav Huna!
phrases.notes: This line closes an argument from before this section: the source seemed to show that one נזירות takes effect on top of another.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes a challenge that started before this section.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that a second נזירות said for the same day does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The source says the second נזירות 'counts' once the first is cancelled, so the second must have taken effect.

steps.title: Two ways to defend רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the source may be talking about 'today' and 'tomorrow,' or about someone who took on two נזירות at once.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. The case really is where he said 'I am a נזיר today, I am a נזיר tomorrow.' When the source says the second one 'counts for him,' it means everything counts except that extra day. Or, the case is where he took on two נזירות at the same moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by reading the earlier source as a different case from his. It gives two possible cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: First answer: he said 'today' and then 'tomorrow,' so the second נזירות could take effect because of the extra day, and 'it counts' means all but that extra day. Second answer: he took on both נזירות in one statement, which is not the case רב הונא was talking about. Either way, the source no longer proves that 'today, today' creates a second נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually; used to say what the case truly is
It counts for him
The extra day
Alternatively, or else
At the same moment, all at once

steps.confusionAlert: The second answer is not the same as saying 'today' twice. Here he took on both נזירות together in one moment, so each one could take effect from the start.

phrases.english: No, actually
the case is 'I am hereby a nazirite today, I am hereby a nazirite tomorrow,'
and what does 'it is counted for him' mean?
phrases.notes: He is quoting the wording of the earlier source, which said the second נזירות counts once the first is cancelled.

phrases.english: Except for that extra day.
phrases.notes: The extra day is 'tomorrow,' which the first נזירות did not cover.

phrases.english: Alternatively,

phrases.aramaic: כְּגוֹן שֶׁקִּיבֵּל שְׁתֵּי נְזִירוּת בְּבַת אַחַת.
phrases.english: it is a case where he accepted two naziriteships at once.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the refutation in step 1 by giving a different case for the source.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The source was about saying 'today, today,' so it would contradict רב הונא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The source is about 'today, tomorrow' (all counts except the extra day) or about two נזירות taken on at once, so it does not contradict רב הונא.

steps.title: רב המנונא brings a ברייתא: נזירות takes effect on נזירות
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא quotes a ברייתא that learns from 'נזיר להזיר' that נזירות takes effect on נזירות, even though a קל וחומר from שבועה would have said it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא challenged: 'נזיר להזיר' teaches that נזירות takes effect on נזירות. You might have thought the opposite by logic: a שבועה is strict, and still one שבועה does not take effect on another שבועה. So נזירות, which is more lenient, should surely not take effect on נזירות! That is why the פסוק says 'נזיר להזיר': to teach that נזירות does take effect on נזירות.
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge to רב הונא begins. רב המנונא quotes a ברייתא that says one נזירות can take effect on top of another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first sets up a קל וחומר: if strict שבועה cannot stack, then lighter נזירות surely cannot. The פסוק 'נזיר להזיר' overrides that logic and teaches that נזירות does stack. This step lays out the source. The next step shows why it hurts רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: Raises an objection from a source
'A נזיר, to set himself apart'; the doubled wording in the פסוק
Takes effect on top of
Reasoning from a stricter case to a lighter one (here: 'וַהֲלֹא דִּין הוּא')
The פסוק comes to teach

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna raised an objection:
'A nazirite, to consecrate himself' —
from here we learn that naziriteship takes effect on naziriteship.
For one might have said, isn't it logical:
if an oath, which is strict —
an oath does not take effect on an oath,
then naziriteship, which is lenient, all the more so should not!
Therefore the verse says: 'A nazirite, to consecrate himself,'
from here we learn that naziriteship takes effect on naziriteship.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first challenge was answered, a new challenge is raised from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's view that a second נזירות for the same day does not take effect.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא says the פסוק teaches that נזירות takes effect on נזירות, against the קל וחומר from שבועה.

steps.title: The ברייתא must be about saying 'today' twice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the ברייתא cannot be about 'today, tomorrow,' since that needs no פסוק. So it must be about 'today, today,' which goes against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he said 'I am a נזיר today, I am a נזיר tomorrow,' do we need a פסוק for that? Rather, isn't it where he said 'I am a נזיר today, I am a נזיר today'? And the ברייתא teaches that נזירות takes effect on נזירות!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks which case the ברייתא means. It concludes that it must be the exact case רב הונא ruled on, which sharpens the challenge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With 'today, tomorrow,' the second נזירות obviously applies because of the extra day, so no פסוק would be needed. Since the ברייתא needs a פסוק, it must be teaching the hard case of 'today, today.' There it says the second נזירות does take effect, the opposite of רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
If you say
Does it need a פסוק?
Rather, isn't it...
And yet it teaches

steps.whatToRemember: A ברייתא learns from 'נזיר להזיר' that נזירות takes effect on נזירות. Since 'today, tomorrow' would not need a פסוק, the ברייתא seems to be about 'today, today,' which challenges רב הונא.
steps.whyThisMatters: The proof rests on a common גמרא tool: if a case is obvious, a פסוק would not be needed for it, so the פסוק must be teaching the less obvious case.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If we say that he said
'I am hereby a nazirite today, I am hereby a nazirite tomorrow,'
does that need a verse?!
phrases.notes: There the second נזירות clearly applies because of the extra day, so no פסוק is needed to teach it.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't it where he said
'I am hereby a nazirite today, I am hereby a nazirite today' —
and it teaches that naziriteship takes effect on naziriteship!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רב המנונא's challenge by pinning down which case the ברייתא is about.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling on 'הריני נזיר היום, הריני נזיר היום'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'today, tomorrow' case needs no פסוק, so the ברייתא must be about 'today, today,' and it says the second נזירות takes effect.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about two נזירות taken in one statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא defends רב הונא: the ברייתא is not about 'today, today' said separately. It is about someone who took on two נזירות at the same moment.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. What case are we dealing with here? A case where he took on two נזירות at once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 4 by giving the ברייתא a different case. It is about one statement that takes on two נזירות together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא holds that a second נזירות said later does not take effect on an existing one. If both are accepted in one statement, there is no 'existing' נזירות yet for the second to land on, so both take effect. That is what the פסוק 'נזיר להזיר' teaches, and רב הונא is not refuted.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? Used to give a source a narrower case.
At one time, together
The vow and state of being a נזיר

phrases.english: No, with what are we dealing here?
For example, where he accepted upon himself
two נזירות at one time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 4's claim that the ברייתא must be about 'today, today' against רב הונא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was thought to describe two separate statements of 'today', which would mean נזירות takes effect on an existing נזירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about two נזירות accepted together, so it does not contradict רב הונא.

steps.title: Why is a שבועה stricter than a נדר?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא assumed a שבועה is stricter than a נדר. The גמרא asks what that extra strictness is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the strictness of a שבועה over a נדר?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's קל וחומר and asks a clarifying question. Why did the ברייתא assume a שבועה is more severe than a נדר? This sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's קל וחומר said: a שבועה does not take effect on a שבועה, so surely a נדר (which is weaker) cannot take effect on a נדר. That only works if a שבועה really is stricter, so the גמרא wants to know in what way.

keyTerms.meaning: Strictness, a more severe side
An oath. It puts the obligation on the person.
A vow. It puts the prohibition on the object.

phrases.english: And what is the strictness of a שבועה over a נדר?
phrases.notes: This goes back to the קל וחומר in the ברייתא from Step 3.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רב הונא debate and examines an assumption inside the ברייתא from Step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: In what way is a שבועה more severe than a נדר, so that the קל וחומר works?

steps.title: Rejecting the idea that a שבועה is stricter because it works on things with no substance
steps.stepSummary: One idea: a שבועה works even on something with no substance. This is rejected, because a נדר also has its own strict side: it works on a מצוה just like on something optional.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because a שבועה takes effect even on something with no substance, a נדר is also strict, since it takes effect on a מצוה just as on something optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests one answer and immediately knocks it down. Each one, שבועה and נדר, has its own strict point, so this cannot prove that a שבועה is stricter overall.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שבועה can apply to something without substance, like 'I will not sleep'. A נדר cannot do that, because it has to apply to an object. But a נדר can forbid an object used for a מצוה, like a סוכה, while a שבועה cannot override a מצוה. Since each one is stricter in a different way, neither is simply 'more severe'.

keyTerms.meaning: If you will say. It opens a suggested answer that will be rejected.
Something with no physical substance, like sleeping or talking
Something optional, neither a מצוה nor forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix them up: the שבועה is the one that works on things without substance, and the נדר is the one that works even on a מצוה.

phrases.english: If you say it is because it takes effect

phrases.aramaic: אֲפִילּוּ עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ,
phrases.english: even on a thing that has no substance,
a נדר is also strict,
since it takes effect on a מצוה just as on something optional.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּחָיְילָא אֲפִילּוּ עַל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ מַמָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a first answer to the question of Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects 'works on things without substance' as the source of the שבועה's extra strictness.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A נדר has a matching strict side, since it works on a מצוה, so the two cancel out.

steps.title: A שבועה is stricter because of 'לֹא יְנַקֶּה'
steps.stepSummary: The real answer: the תורה writes 'לֹא יְנַקֶּה' about a שבועה, which shows a special severity.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because it is written about a שבועה: 'He will not hold guiltless.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer. A שבועה is stricter because the תורה adds a special warning about it: 'לֹא יְנַקֶּה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about taking ה׳'s name in vain says ה׳ 'will not hold guiltless' the one who does it. A שבועה is made with ה׳'s name, so breaking it carries this extra severity. A נדר does not have this warning, so the ברייתא's קל וחומר stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'He will not hold guiltless'. This is the extra severity of a false שבועה.

steps.whatToRemember: A שבועה counts as stricter than a נדר because of 'לֹא יְנַקֶּה', not because it works on things without substance. A נדר has its own strict side, since it works on a מצוה.

phrases.english: Rather, because it is written about it, about a שבועה:
"He will not hold guiltless."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב בָּהּ בִּשְׁבוּעָה לֹא יְנַקֶּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of Step 7 with the accepted one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A שבועה is stricter because the תורה says 'לֹא יְנַקֶּה' about it.

steps.title: The משנה: two identical שבועות give only one liability
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: someone who said 'שבועה שלא אוכל' twice and then ate is liable only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'An oath that I will not eat, an oath that I will not eat,' and he ate: he is liable only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה about repeating the same שבועה. This sets up רבא's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since he already swore not to eat, the second שבועה adds nothing new. So when he eats, he brings only one קרבן. The question that follows is whether the second שבועה is completely empty or only on hold.

keyTerms.meaning: 'An oath that I will not eat'
He is liable only once

phrases.english: "An oath that I will not eat,
an oath that I will not eat," and he ate:
he is liable for only one.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אוֹכַל שְׁבוּעָה שֶׁלֹּא אוֹכַל וְאָכַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new section that quotes the משנה. It connects to the same theme of one obligation landing on another.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Repeating the same שבועה creates only one liability.

steps.title: רבא: if the first שבועה is released, the second takes effect
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that if the person asks a חכם to release the first שבועה, the second one takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: If he asked to release the first one, the second takes effect on him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא adds a new law to the משנה. The second שבועה is not empty, it is waiting, and it kicks in once the first is removed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second שבועה could not take effect at first because the first one already covered eating. Once the first is cancelled through שאלה לחכם, the space is open, and the second שבועה now binds him.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a חכם to release his שבועה (התרה)
Takes effect on him

phrases.english: רבא said:
If he asked about the first one,
phrases.notes: He went to a חכם and had the first שבועה released.

phrases.english: the second takes effect on him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא אִם נִשְׁאַל עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ruling to the משנה quoted in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A second identical שבועה is on hold. If the first is released, the second takes effect.

steps.title: Proof from the משנה's wording: 'liable for only one', not 'only one'
steps.stepSummary: רבא's source: the משנה says 'he is liable only once', not 'there is only one'. This means the second שבועה exists but just has no room, and it takes effect once the first is released.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where? Since it does not say 'there is only one' but says 'he is liable for only one', the second just has no room. When he asks about the other one, it takes effect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבא learned this, and proves it from the exact wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second שבועה were meaningless, the משנה would have said 'there is only one שבועה'. Instead it talks only about liability, which hints that the second שבועה is real but has no space yet. Once the first is removed, the space opens and the second takes effect.

keyTerms.meaning: From where? What is the source?
Room, space for it to take effect
Its companion, the other שבועה

phrases.english: From where do we know this?
Since it does not teach "it is only one,"
but teaches "he is liable for only one,"
it is room that it does not have.
phrases.notes: Meaning the second שבועה is real; it just has no space to take effect yet.

phrases.english: When he asks about its companion, it takes effect.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי מִדְּלָא קָתָנֵי אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רבא's ruling in Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that the second שבועה takes effect after the first is released
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה's wording 'אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב אֶלָּא אַחַת' rather than 'אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא אַחַת'

steps.title: Another version: no liability, but the שבועה still exists
steps.stepSummary: A second version of the proof: the משנה only denies the liability, which implies the second שבועה does exist.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another version: it is the liability that is missing, but the שבועה is there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of how רבא's idea comes from the משנה. Here the משנה's wording itself tells us the second שבועה exists. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first version said the second שבועה simply lacks room. This version reads the משנה more directly: only the חיוב is missing, so the שבועה itself is present. That raises the question of what difference an existing שבועה makes.

keyTerms.meaning: Another version of the discussion
Liability, the obligation to bring a קרבן

phrases.english: Another version:
it is liability that there is not,
but there is a שבועה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Presents a second version of the inference from the משנה, parallel to Step 11.

steps.title: What difference does the second שבועה make?
steps.stepSummary: If there is no liability, what law comes out of the second שבועה existing?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick clarifying question. If the second שבועה brings no liability, why does it matter that it exists? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שבועה with no practical result would be meaningless. So the גמרא looks for the practical difference.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? What is the practical difference?

phrases.english: For what law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the practical result of the inference in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What practical law follows from the second שבועה existing?

steps.title: The difference is רבא's rule: the second replaces the first
steps.stepSummary: The difference is רבא's rule. If the first שבועה is released, the second takes its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבא's rule, since רבא said: If he asked about the first, the second rises up in its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the existing second שבועה matters for רבא's rule. Once the first is released, the second steps in and takes its place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both versions reach the same law, but they build it in opposite directions. In the first version, רבא states his rule and the גמרא then finds its source in the משנה's wording. In the second version, the גמרא starts from the משנה's wording, which implies the second שבועה exists, and then uses רבא's rule to explain what practical difference that makes.

keyTerms.meaning: It goes up and counts for him
In its place

steps.whatToRemember: Two identical שבועות give only one liability. But the second one is real and waiting: if the first is released by a חכם, the second takes its place (רבא).

phrases.english: For that of רבא.
As רבא said:
If he asked about the first one,
the second counts for him in its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְכִדְרָבָא דְּאָמַר רָבָא נִשְׁאַל עַל הָרִאשׁוֹנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13 using רבא's rule from Step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The second שבועה matters because it takes the place of the first if the first is released.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In both versions, רבא's rule stands: a released first שבועה lets the second take effect in its place.

steps.title: A case of two נזירות seems to support רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a case where someone vowed two נזירות and later released the first. The second term then counts in place of the first, which looks just like רבא's rule.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say a source supports רבא: if a person vowed two terms of נזירות, counted the days of the first term, set aside his קרבן, and then asked a חכם to release the first term, the second term counts for him in place of the first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests that an existing teaching about נזירות supports רבא's rule from the earlier steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the second נזירות could not start right away, because the first one was already in force. Once the first was released, the days he already counted are credited to the second term. That looks exactly like רבא's idea: the second vow was waiting in the background and stepped in once the first was removed.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us say this supports him. The גמרא is offering a possible proof.
A vow to be a נזיר, which forbids wine, haircuts and contact with the dead for a set time.
He counted the days of the term.
He set aside the offering a נזיר brings at the end of his term.
He asked a חכם to release his vow.
It counts for him, meaning he gets credit for it.

phrases.english: Let us say this supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רבא, whose rule we just learned: when the first שבועה is released, the second takes effect.

phrases.english: One who vowed two terms of naziriteship
and counted the first term,
and set aside an offering
and asked to be released from it
the second counts for him in place of the first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings outside support for רבא's rule, which was explained in Step 14.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's rule that once the first שבועה is released, the second one takes effect.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching about someone who vowed two נזירות: when the first is released, the second counts in its place.

steps.title: The proof is pushed away: both נזירות were accepted at once
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the נזירות case is about someone who took on both terms at the same moment. In that case the second term is a real vow from the start. It does not show that a second שבועה with no room can wake up later.
steps.simpleTranslation: No proof: that case is where he accepted both terms of נזירות at one time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the נזירות case by explaining it differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When a person accepts two terms of נזירות together, both take effect right away. They just run one after the other, so the second term is fully valid and is simply waiting its turn. A second שבועה on something already forbidden by a שבועה is different: it has no room at all, so the נזירות case cannot prove רבא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: For example; here it means 'the case is one where.'
He took upon himself.
At one time, together.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the גמרא is saying רבא is wrong. It only says this particular case does not prove him, because two נזירות can line up one after the other, while two שבועות on the same thing cannot.

phrases.english: The case is where he accepted upon himself
two terms of naziriteship at one time.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּגוֹן שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו שְׁתֵּי נְזִירוֹת בְּבַת אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in Step 15 by reading the case as a special situation.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the נזירות case. רבא's rule itself is left standing.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed the second נזירות had no room, like a second שבועה. But when both were accepted together, the second was valid from the start and simply followed the first, so the cases are not alike.
